conclusion.headline: All Conv2 surfaces remain boundary-unresolved; five form the requested expansion batch.
conclusion.observation: All six Conv2 surfaces produced a passing diagnostic core candidate between 95.70% and 97.78% final validation accuracy, but every passing 2% loss plateau touches an upper rho boundary. Only baseline SGD was published before the selector failed; the other five decisions are read-only reconstructions.
conclusion.interpretation: The high three-epoch accuracies support testing the next factor-of-three rho values, not freezing the current candidates. The 97.78% legacy-Adam row is still boundary-unresolved and lies outside the requested five-surface continuation. The user-fixed gain 100 and T/K 6/6 remain ordinary-MNIST diagnostic inputs.
conclusion.decision: Keep the core evidence as a reviewed diagnostic. Continue only with the requested Conv2 baseline and ours surfaces under SGD and Adam plus legacy SGD, adding rho_conv=0.027 and rho_dense=0.09 as specified. Freeze no learning rate before final selection.
limitations: Ordinary MNIST rather than deterministic medium affine MNIST.
Three-epoch optimizer screen rather than authorized final training.
Five of six selector decisions are read-only reconstructions.
All six surfaces remain on a search boundary.
The official test set was not read.

claims.statement: The Conv2 shard contains a hash-verified completion chain for all 53 promoted core candidates.
Read-only application of the intended selector marks all six Conv2 surfaces as needing an upward rho expansion.
The requested continuation contains baseline and ours under both optimizers plus legacy SGD, with up to seven new cells per surface.
Legacy Adam has the highest observed Conv2 core validation accuracy at 97.78%, but its loss plateau remains boundary-unresolved.
This incomplete ordinary-MNIST core screen does not freeze a Conv2 learning rate or support a final-paper accuracy claim.
